- Slightly flatter is allowed only if flow depth is 0.3 of the diameter or more.
- Lay to plan grade; flag any plan grade flatter than 0.40% to the foreman.

Plug and brace every pipe, seal a test head on top, pull 10 in Hg, then time the drop to 9 in Hg (ASTM C1244). [1][3]

1. Plug and brace all pipes with pneumatic plugs.
2. Seal the test head on a clean top.
3. Pull 10 in Hg, close the valve, shut off the pump.
4. Time 10 to 9 in Hg; it passes if the time meets the table for its size and depth.
5. If it fails, repair the leak and retest.

- HI = 100.00 + 4.25 = 104.25 ft, and elevation = HI − foresight (104.25 − 6.75) [1][6].

text:
Treat it as heat stroke: call 911 now and start cooling him.
1. Call 911 (or your site emergency number) now; confusion is a heat stroke sign.
2. Move him to shade or an air-conditioned truck, out of the trench if safe.
3. Strip heavy and outer clothing; soak him with cool water, put cold wet cloths on head, neck, armpits and groin, and fan him.
4. Cold water or ice-bath immersion up to the neck is best, if you can.
5. Stay with him, keep cooling until EMS takes over, and give no fluids while he's confused.
6. If he stops breathing, start CPR.
q: Guy is confused and stumbling and its 100 out. What do I do?

If someone is down, not responding, trapped, or a gas alarm is going off:
- Get out yourself and keep everyone else out.
- Do NOT go in after them unless you are a trained, equipped rescuer. Untrained rescuers are often the next victims.
- Call 911 or your emergency number now, then tell your supervisor / entry supervisor.
- If a permit is open, use EMERGENCY so the entry team and the permit record know.

In Texas (federal OSHA applies), a protective system such as a trench box, shoring or sloping is required at 5 ft deep or more, unless the excavation is entirely in stable rock (29 CFR 1926.652(a)(1)).
- Under 5 ft still needs one if the ground shows any sign of cave-in.
- Your competent person decides on site.

- Stable rock is the only exception.

- Maintenance work falls under 1910.146; a mixed employer follows Subpart AA.

In California, a trench 5 feet deep or deeper needs a protective system (sloping, benching, shoring or a trench box) unless it is cut entirely in stable rock (8 CCR 1541.1(a)(1); federal 29 CFR 1926.652(a)(1) is the same).
- Under 5 ft still needs one if there is any sign the ground could cave in.
- California also requires a Cal/OSHA permit for trenches 5 ft or deeper that a person enters.
- Your competent person decides on site.

In California, the oxygen range to test for is 19.5 to 23.5 percent, the same as federal OSHA (29 CFR 1910.146 App. E; 8 CCR 1950-1962).
- Below 19.5% is deficient and above 23.5% is enriched (fire hazard).
- An in-range O2 reading alone doesn't clear entry; LEL, H2S and CO must be tested too.
- Your competent person decides on site.

The fall is 1.25 ft over 250 ft at 0.5% slope [3].

- Percent grade is feet of fall per 100 ft, so 0.5 ft per 100 ft [3].
- 1.25 ft is 0.0050 ft per ft times 250 ft [6].

In Texas, a pipeline locate ticket is good for 14 working days unless you and the operator agree otherwise in writing (16 TAC 18.1, 18.3, 18.4).
- Weekends and legal holidays don't count as working days.
- If the work isn't finished, refresh the ticket for the area still to dig.

On a pipe they are effectively the same thing: the invert is the lowest inside point of the pipe, and the flowline is the line along those inverts [1].
- Plan elevations for gravity pipe are almost always inverts; stakes may print INV, IE or FL [2].
- Neither is the outside bottom of pipe (BOP), which sits one wall thickness lower [1].
